learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to write a foolproof Business Plan, choose the right form of business organization, and lay out your operational strategies!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A comprehensively written down document prepared by the entrepreneur describing formally all the relevant external and internal elements involved in starting a new venture. It is a roadmap!
Choosing the legal structure of your business. The main types are Sole Proprietorship (one owner), Partnership (2 or more owners), and Joint Stock Company (shares, separate legal entity).
Details how the product will be manufactured or how the service will be provided. It includes location, manufacturing process, machinery required, and raw materials.
Identifies the personnel needs of the business. It details how many employees are needed, what skills they should have, and how they will be trained and compensated.
The most critical part for investors! It projects the financial requirements, sources of funds, cash flow statements, and break-even analysis.

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The Elevator Pitch
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you step into an elevator with a billionaire investor. You have exactly 60 seconds to explain your business idea, who your customer is, and why it will make money. Write out your pitch!

exam_tips: 📌 A Business Plan is often called the 'road map' of a venture—use this phrase in your answers.
📌 Clearly distinguish between the 'Unlimited Liability' of a sole proprietor and the 'Limited Liability' of company shareholders.
📌 Be prepared to list the contents of a standard Business Plan (Executive summary, marketing plan, financial plan, etc.).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Executive Summary is written last but appears first in the Business Plan.
⭐ A Sole Proprietorship is the easiest to form but holds the highest personal financial risk.
⭐ A well-drafted business plan is essential for raising capital from banks and investors.
